name: Crowing Crested Cobra
body:
CROWING CRESTED COBRA
CR 7

This long snake with pale scales has a frilled crest arising from the top of its head.

XP 3,200
NE Huge magical beast
Init +3; Senses blindsight 30 ft., darkvision 60 ft., low-light vision, tremorsense 60 ft.; Perception +14

DEFENSE

AC 20, touch 11, flat-footed 17 (+3 Dex, +9 natural, –2 size)
hp 85 (10d10+30)
Fort +10, Ref +10, Will +6

OFFENSE

Speed 60 ft., swim 60 ft.
Melee bite +16 (2d6+10/19–20 plus poison)
Space 15 ft.; Reach 10 ft.
Special Attacks poison, potent venom, virulent venom

STATISTICS

Str 24, Dex 16, Con 16, Int 10, Wis 13, Cha 5
Base Atk +10; CMB +19; CMD 32
Feats Ability Focus (poison), Improved Critical (bite), Iron Will, Vital Strike, Weapon Focus (bite)
Skills Climb +10, Perception +14, Stealth +6 (+10 in jungles and marshes), Swim +18; Racial Modifiers +4 Stealth in jungles and marshes
Languages Common (can’t speak)
SQ mimicry

SPECIAL ABILITIES

Mimicry (Ex)

The crowing crested cobra can mimic the sounds of animals it has eaten. Creatures hearing the sounds can identify them as fake with a successful DC 20 Survival check.

Poison (Ex)

Bite; save Fort DC 20; frequency 1/round for 6 rounds; effect 1d4 Con; cure 2 consecutive saves.

Potent Venom (Su)

The venom of a crowing crested cobra is particularly potent. Living creatures that normally have a bonus that specifically applies on saving throws against poison lose that bonus against the cobra’s venom, and creatures without such bonuses instead take a -2 penalty on their saves vs. poison (including that of the cobra) for 1 minute after being bitten; this penalty does not stack with multiple bites. Delay poison has no effect on the cobra’s venom unless the cast succeeds on a DC 18 caster level check.

Virulent Venom (Ex)

The cobra’s venom is so toxic that living creatures take 3d6 damage each time they fail their save against its poison. Those succeeding on their saves take half damage.

ECOLOGY

Environment warm forest or marsh
Organization solitary
Treasure standard

Crowing crested cobras are large venomous snakes with malicious intellects. They resemble hoodless cobras with the wattle or crest of a chicken or rooster. Their capabilities resemble those of other extremely large venomous snakes, though they have unusually powerful venom and move quite swiftly. It’s their intelligence, however, approaching that of a typical human, that makes them incredibly dangerous.

Crowing crested cobras can mimic the sounds of common and domesticated animals, such as chickens, roosters, crows, and goats. Legends tell that it can mimic the sounds of any animal it has eaten, though none have ever been encountered that can speak like a person. Crowing crested cobras use these vocalizations to lure and trap small animals and people, who mistake it for a lost goat or chicken, or a harmless crow.

The skin, bones, fangs, venom, eyes, and other parts of the crowing crested cobra are valuable to spellcasters and alchemists, who use them to increase the potency of spells and potions.

Crowing crested cobras go out of their way to hunt and kill people and animals. Unlike other large snakes, which might be considered “mean” but are not truly cruel, crowing crested cobras toy with their prey, and they often hunt and kill people and domesticated animals, even when they aren’t hungry and their prey is long distances away from their nest.
